user.description: Pick the location to report precipitation for. DWD's radar only covers Germany and a narrow band beyond its borders.

data_description.name: Used for the device and as the prefix of every entity id.
data_description.coordinates: The sensors report the radar grid cell containing this point, roughly 1 km across.

error.name_already_exists: An entry with this name already exists. Please choose a different name.
error.coordinates_out_of_range: This integration only provides data for Germany. The selected location is outside the covered area.

init.title: DWD Precipitation options
init.description: The settings are grouped by the sensors they change. Saving reloads the integration; the sensors are back after a few seconds. [What each setting does]({docs_url}/getting-started/configuration#options)

data_description.precipitation_threshold: Lighter rain counts as dry for these three sensors. 0 counts any rain the radar sees; about 0.5 ignores drizzle.
data_description.start_end_mode: Whichever you do not pick is still shown as an attribute of the two sensors.
data_description.precipitation_end_algorithm: “The first dry break” is when the current shower stops, so in showery weather it can change often. “When no more rain is forecast” changes less often, but stays “unknown” for longer. The forecast reaches 2 hours ahead. [More about both]({docs_url}/getting-started/configuration#end-algorithm)

dry_streak.name: Timespan without precipitation
dry_streak.description: For the sensor that counts how long it has not rained.

data_description.precipitation_reset_threshold: When at least this much rain falls within one hour, the count starts again from zero. 1 mm is 1 litre per square metre.
data_description.dry_streak_source: With radar and rain gauges the count is more accurate, but a reset shows about 30 to 40 minutes after the rain. Radar only reacts within a few minutes, but is less exact. [More about both]({docs_url}/getting-started/configuration#dry-streak-source)

rain_event_tracking.name: Rain events and rain warnings
rain_event_tracking.description: Rain events follow each shower from the first forecast that shows it until it has passed. Rain warnings are built on them; you add those with “Add rain warning” on this integration's page.

data_description.rain_events: For blueprints that warn about or report rain. Rain warnings work without it. While the sensor or a rain warning is in use, the integration keeps a small record of recent rain. [About the sensor]({docs_url}/entities/rain-events)
data_description.rain_event_threshold: Applies to the “Rain events” sensor and to all rain warnings. 0 counts any rain the radar sees. Separate from the setting of the same name under “Rain forecast”.

advanced_options.name: Advanced
advanced_options.description: Extra details for templates and charts, and what the sensors show when DWD is late. Most installations never change these.

data.extra_state_attributes: Add technical details to the sensors
data.full_rolling_series: Add the past hour to the hourly rain series
data.unavailable_when_stale: Show “unavailable” when the data is out of date

data_description.extra_state_attributes: Shows which DWD product each value comes from, when it was measured and which period it covers, as extra attributes. Helpful when you report a problem; otherwise leave it off. [List of the details]({docs_url}/entities/attributes#technical-details)
data_description.full_rolling_series: For charts: the “forecast_rolling_1h” attribute of “Peak hourly precipitation next 120 min” then starts an hour earlier, so rain that has already fallen and the forecast form one curve. The sensor's value does not change. After a restart, the past hour fills in over the first hour. [More]({docs_url}/entities/radvor-rv#peak-hourly-precipitation)
data_description.unavailable_when_stale: When DWD is late with new data, the affected sensors show “unavailable” instead of an old value. Turn this off to keep showing the last value, even if it is hours old. Either way, new data is fetched as soon as DWD publishes it. [When data counts as out of date]({docs_url}/how-it-works/availability)

user.title: Add a rain warning
user.description: A rain warning turns on shortly before rain reaches this location, and stays on while it rains. Each warning is a device of its own, named after the location and the warning (“Home Laundry”), with two entities: “Rain warning” (on/off) and “Rain warning status” (dry, soon or rain, with the details of the rain event). It works on the rain events the integration tracks, so the advanced option “Rain event threshold” decides what counts as rain.

data.name: Name
data.min_peak_1h: Minimum rain in the wettest hour (mm)
data.min_peak_10min: Minimum rain in the wettest 10 minutes (mm)

data_description.name: What the warning is for, such as “Laundry” or “Windows”. At a location named “Home”, “Laundry” gives the device “Home Laundry” and binary_sensor.home_laundry_rain_warning.
data_description.lead_time: How many minutes before the rain the warning turns on. The forecast reaches two hours ahead and arrives a few minutes after DWD's release, so the warning can come up to 5 minutes later than this.
data_description.min_mm: Only warn about a rain event that brings at least this much in total, measured and forecast. Leave empty to warn about every rain event.
data_description.min_peak_1h: Only warn about a rain event whose wettest hour brings at least this much. Leave empty to ignore it.
data_description.min_peak_10min: Only warn about a rain event whose wettest 10 minutes bring at least this much, for short heavy bursts. Leave empty to ignore it.
data_description.combine: Whether an event has to reach one of the minimums you set, or all of them. Without a minimum it does not matter.

reconfigure.title: Change the rain warning
reconfigure.description: A new name renames the warning's device and entities; their entity ids stay as they are.
